title: One evaluator for items delivered together, with per-item attempts and receipts
outcome: A requester can have one evaluator judge several items that were delivered together; each item keeps its own attempt, its own record and its own receipt, and the evaluator can address only the items the host allowlisted for it.
acceptance: A requester can have one evaluator session judge several items it lists; for each item the host checks eligibility on its own and keeps its own attempt key, bases, source, policy, task pin and receipt; a test shows two items judged by one evaluator with two records.
An evaluator's submission names exactly one item, and only an item on the list the host gave that evaluator; a submission for any other item is refused; a test shows the refusal.

One item's result never satisfies another: an item that was refused, or whose newest record does not pass, is reported to the requester by itself and the others are unaffected; a test shows a mixed outcome.
TermAl's specification of the host's acceptance-evaluation procedure describes this and links Engram's section 'Evaluation unit and re-evaluation'.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree, its run directory and fingerprint cited in a note.
The host bounds the number of items one evaluator session may serve, states the number in its specification, and spawns a further evaluator beyond it; a test shows the bound.
